newsitem.title: USA: Smithfield says N. Carolina hog plant up Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Smithfield says N. Carolina hog plant up Saturday.

text.p: Smithfield Food's hog plant in Tar Heel, N.C., received minor roof damage and lost power from Hurricane Fran, but was expected to be operating by Saturday, a company official said.
"We lost electricity, but we've got full on-site generating capacity so it will be business as usual, if we can just get the people in the plant," said Robert Manly, executive vice president.
Manly said main roads were open, but side roads remain cluttered with downed trees, which was making it difficult for employees to get to the plant.
Manly said the company plans to run two shifts Saturday, depending on how many employees come in.
We're in a position to run the plant full from a hog supply and plant operation perspective," Manly said.

The plant did receive minor roof damage in a corner of a "non-production" area, but placement of a tarp over the damage will allow the company to resume operations until full repairs can be made, Manly said.
Manly declined to give the plant's hog slaughter capacity, but industry sources said the Tar Heel facility can slaughter up to 24,000 hogs a day using two shifts.
